name: Quorum Biofilm
description: Bacterial collective intelligence via quorum sensing — chemical autoinducers trigger coordinated behavior at population density threshold. Biofilm architecture with division of labor and matrix shielding. Horizontal gene transfer enables rapid adaptation.

core_attributes.pattern: density-threshold signaling, biofilm matrix construction, horizontal gene transfer

scope.definition: Quorum sensing coordination accuracy — fraction of genes in the biofilm regulon that are co-expressed within 5 minutes of autoinducer concentration crossing threshold, as fraction of total regulated genes.

evidence.source: Fuqua & Greenberg (2002) 'Listening in on bacteria: acyl-homoserine lactone signalling', Nature Reviews Molecular Cell Biology 3:685-695; Waters & Bassler (2005) 'Quorum sensing', Annual Review of Cell and Developmental Biology 21:319-346.
cross_domain_examples: V. fischeri quorum: 91% of regulated genes co-induced within 3 minutes of lux operon threshold crossing
P. aeruginosa biofilm: quorum coordinates virulence factor expression with 0.88 gene regulon synchrony
circadian gene expression in mammals: analogous population-synchronized transcriptional switching

scope.falsifiability: If individual bacterial cells in established biofilm show uncorrelated gene expression timing (R² <0.30) relative to quorum threshold, synchronization is not operating at the population level.
scope.measurement_limits: Synchrony decreases at biofilm edges where autoinducer concentrations are diluted. Mass-transfer limitations in thick biofilms (>100 µm) create spatial gradients that reduce synchronization fidelity.
